title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Software Engineering (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Software Engineering (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following principles of cyber security refers that the security mechanism must be as small and simple as possible?
questions.explanation: The Economy of Mechanism principle states that security mechanisms should be as simple and small as possible to reduce potential vulnerabilities and make verification easier. This principle is crucial because complex security mechanisms are more likely to contain flaws and are harder to verify for correctness.

questions.questionText: What is the maximum number of swaps that can be performed in the Selection Sort algorithm?
questions.explanation: In Selection Sort, the maximum number of swaps is n-1 because after sorting n-1 elements, the last element is automatically in its correct position. This is because Selection Sort works by repeatedly finding the minimum element from the unsorted part and putting it at the beginning. After n-1 iterations, the last element is already in its correct position.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: C++ is an object-oriented programming language;
Java is an object-oriented programming language;
the object-oriented approach does not separate the behavior of a system from the data;
Java is the only object-oriented programming language;
questions.explanation: Java is not the only object-oriented programming language. There are many others like C++, Python, C#, Ruby, and Smalltalk. Object-oriented programming is a paradigm supported by numerous languages, each with their own features and implementations of OOP concepts.

questions.questionText: Why is it important to maintain a good relationship between software testers and developers?
options: To ensure that the project is completed on time
To foster collaboration and communication between the two teams
To make sure that the software is defect-free
To reduce the cost of the project
questions.explanation: Good relationships foster better collaboration and communication, which leads to more effective testing and higher quality software. This collaboration helps in early defect detection, better understanding of requirements, and more efficient problem-solving, ultimately improving the overall software quality and development process.

questions.questionText: Which layer is responsible for wireless signal encoding and frequency band definition?
questions.explanation: The Medium Access Control (MAC) layer handles wireless signal encoding and frequency band definition in wireless networks. It manages how devices access the shared wireless medium, controls data transmission, and handles collision avoidance, making it crucial for wireless communication.

questions.questionText: Which of the following qualities can most likely be improved by using a layered architecture?
options: Flexibility in modifying or changing the system
questions.explanation: Layered architecture improves modifiability and flexibility in changing the system as layers can be modified independently. This separation of concerns allows for easier maintenance, testing, and evolution of the system, as changes in one layer typically don't affect other layers.

questions.questionText: The software requirement specification(SRS) is said to be ______ if and only if no subset of individual requirements described in it conflict with each other
questions.explanation: Consistency in SRS means there are no conflicts between requirements. This is crucial because inconsistent requirements can lead to implementation conflicts, increased development time, and potential system failures. A consistent SRS ensures that all requirements can be implemented together without contradictions.

questions.questionText: Why is Software architecture so important?
questions.explanation: Software architecture is important for all these reasons: communication, early decisions, and providing a system abstraction. It serves as a blueprint for the system, helps in making critical design decisions early, facilitates communication between stakeholders, and provides a high-level view of the system that can be transferred and understood by different teams.

questions.questionText: How can we stop the services in android?
options: By using the stopSelf() and stopService() method
questions.explanation: Android services are stopped using stopSelf() (from within the service) or stopService() (from outside the service). These methods ensure proper cleanup of resources and prevent memory leaks. The finish() method is for activities, and system.exit() should never be used in Android as it can cause application instability.

questions.questionText: You try to analyze your architecture quantitatively. Which is the most appropriate indicators for architectural problem areas?
options: Names of public methods do not reflect their purpose
Number of test cases per component
questions.explanation: High coupling between components is a strong quantitative indicator of architectural problems. It leads to reduced maintainability, increased complexity, and makes the system more difficult to modify. While the other options are important, they are more qualitative in nature and don't provide the same level of measurable architectural insight.

questions.questionText: Polymorphism means:
options: declaring all the methods of a class as public
declaring all the attributes of a class as private
hiding of information so that it is not accessible to other classes
having methods or operators with the same name performing different functions
questions.explanation: Polymorphism in OOP refers to the ability of methods/operators to have multiple forms with the same name. It allows objects of different classes to be treated as objects of a common superclass, enabling code reusability and flexibility. There are two main types: compile-time (method overloading) and runtime (method overriding) polymorphism.

questions.questionText: What is the use of a content provider in Android?
options: For storing the data in the database
For sharing the data between applications
For sending the data from an application to another application
questions.explanation: Content providers in Android are primarily used to share data between applications. They provide a standardized interface for accessing and modifying data, ensuring secure data sharing between different apps while maintaining data integrity and security. They abstract the underlying data storage mechanism and provide a consistent way to access data.

questions.questionText: For a Binary relationships set R between entity sets A and B, the ______ express the number of entities to which another entity can be associated
questions.explanation: Cardinality ratio defines the number of entity instances that can be associated with another entity in a relationship. It specifies the maximum number of relationships an entity can participate in, such as one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many relationships. This is crucial for database design and understanding entity relationships.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following pair of algorithms has equal cost in terms of time and space complexity under equal success function cost?
questions.explanation: DFS and BFS both have O(b^d) time and space complexity where b is branching factor and d is depth. However, it's important to note that while their worst-case complexities are the same, their actual performance can differ significantly based on the problem structure. BFS is complete and optimal for unweighted graphs, while DFS is not complete and may not find the optimal solution.

questions.questionText: Which is the most important feature of spiral model?
questions.explanation: The spiral model emphasizes risk analysis and risk management at each phase of development. It combines elements of both design and prototyping-in-stages, making it particularly useful for large, complex projects where risks need to be identified and mitigated early. Each spiral cycle includes risk assessment and management activities.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the main goal of software testing as part of the quality assurance process?
options: To monitor the software development lifecycle
To control the cost of software development
To ensure that the software meets the specified requirements
To manage project timelines and deadlines
questions.explanation: The primary goal of testing is to verify that the software meets its specified requirements. This includes identifying defects, ensuring functionality, validating performance, and confirming that the software behaves as expected. While other options are important aspects of software development, they are not the primary goal of testing.

questions.questionText: An algorithm that calls itself directly or indirectly is known as
questions.explanation: Recursion is when an algorithm calls itself either directly or indirectly. It's a powerful programming technique that breaks down complex problems into simpler subproblems. Each recursive call must have a base case to terminate the recursion, and the problem must be reducible to smaller instances of the same problem.

questions.questionText: What is supervised learning in AI?
options: Reinforcing learning with a reward-based system
Training a machine learning model with labeled data
Training a machine learning model with unlabeled data
questions.explanation: Supervised learning uses labeled training data to learn mapping from inputs to outputs. The model learns from examples where both input data and correct output are provided, allowing it to make predictions on new, unseen data. This is different from unsupervised learning (which uses unlabeled data) and reinforcement learning (which uses reward signals).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a function of operating system?
options: Translate high level programming language into machine code
Make the computer system convenient to use
questions.explanation: Translating high-level languages is the job of compilers/interpreters, not the OS. The operating system's main functions include process management, memory management, file system management, device management, and providing a user interface. It acts as an intermediary between hardware and software applications.

questions.questionText: The ______ address needs to be looked up in order to deliver a message to the appropriate application software running on a host.
questions.explanation: Port numbers identify specific applications/services running on a host. They enable multiple services to run on the same host by providing unique identifiers for each service. While IP addresses identify hosts, port numbers identify the specific application or service within that host that should receive the message.

questions.questionText: What is Inter process communication?
options: allows processes to communicate and synchronize their actions when using the same address space
allows processes to communicate and synchronize their actions without using the same address space
allows the processes to only synchronize their actions without communication
questions.explanation: IPC enables processes to communicate and synchronize without sharing address space. It provides mechanisms for processes to exchange data and coordinate their activities, even when they run in separate address spaces. Common IPC methods include pipes, message queues, shared memory, and sockets.

The code performs right rotations on the array by moving elements from end to beginning. For each rotation, it removes the last element using pop() and adds it to the beginning using unshift(). This effectively rotates the array right by the specified number of positions. The correct answer shows the array after one right rotation.

questions.questionText: If every requirement can be checked by a cost effective process, then SRS is called
questions.explanation: Verifiable SRS means requirements can be validated through cost-effective methods. This ensures that each requirement can be tested or verified without excessive cost or effort. Verifiability is crucial for ensuring that requirements are testable and can be validated during the testing phase of software development.

questions.questionText: The purpose of foreign key is to identify a particular row of ______.
questions.explanation: A foreign key references a primary key in another (parent/referenced) table. It establishes and enforces a link between data in two tables, ensuring referential integrity. The foreign key in the child table must match a primary key value in the parent table, creating a relationship between the tables.

questions.questionText: When a thread is running, it can return directly to the READY state by which of the following means?
options: by encountering a yield command in a program
by encountering a sleep command in a program
by encountering a wait command in a program
by becoming blocked as a result of an output device being unavailable
questions.explanation: yield() voluntarily gives up CPU, moving thread from running to ready state. This allows other threads of the same priority to execute. Unlike sleep() or wait(), which move threads to blocked state, yield() simply gives up the current time slice and returns to the ready queue, maintaining the thread's ability to be scheduled again immediately.

questions.questionText: Several architecture development methods suggest a view-based approach. Which of the following views are most often used?
questions.explanation: Component view is fundamental in most architecture development methods.

questions.questionText: is Accept risk occurrence but don't do anything about it.
questions.explanation: Risk retention means accepting the risk without taking action to mitigate it.

questions.questionText: ICMP is mostly employed for
questions.explanation: ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) is primarily used for error reporting and diagnostics.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following "sentences" best describe the current explosion of
options: Too much knowledge and too much data
Too much data and too much opportunity
too much data too little knowledge
questions.explanation: This refers to the big data challenge where we have abundant data but struggle to extract meaningful knowledge.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a state in the service lifecycle?
questions.explanation: Service lifecycle states typically include created, running, paused, stopped, destroyed, but not 'Start'.

questions.questionText: What does NULL mean in SQL?
questions.explanation: In SQL, NULL represents an unknown or missing value. It is not the same as zero or an empty string. NULL is a special marker that indicates the absence of a value or that a value is unknown. It is important to note that NULL is not equal to NULL in SQL comparisons, and special operators like IS NULL or IS NOT NULL must be used to check for NULL values.

questions.questionText: Which sorting algorithm has the best average-case time complexity?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort has the best average-case time complexity of O(n log n) among the given options. This is because it uses a divide-and-conquer approach, consistently dividing the input into halves and merging them in sorted order. While other algorithms like Bubble Sort and Insertion Sort have O(n²) average-case complexity, Merge Sort maintains its efficient performance regardless of the input data's initial order.

questions.questionText: What is adaptive maintenance in software engineering?
options: Modifying software to work in a new environment
Adding new features to the software
questions.explanation: Adaptive maintenance involves modifying software to make it work in a new environment or with new requirements, without changing its functionality. This includes changes to accommodate new hardware, operating systems, or other environmental factors. It's different from corrective maintenance (fixing bugs), perfective maintenance (improving performance), and perfective maintenance (adding new features).

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of acknowledgments in TCP?
questions.explanation: Acknowledgments in TCP are used to ensure reliable data delivery. When a receiver successfully receives a segment, it sends an acknowledgment (ACK) back to the sender. If the sender doesn't receive an ACK within a certain time period, it assumes the packet was lost and retransmits it. This mechanism is crucial for TCP's reliability, ensuring that data is delivered correctly and in order.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT part of the test implementation and execution phase?
questions.explanation: Analyzing requirements is not part of the test implementation and execution phase. This phase focuses on the actual testing activities: creating test cases based on already analyzed requirements, executing those test cases, and reporting the results. Requirement analysis typically occurs earlier in the software development lifecycle, during the planning and design phases.

questions.questionText: Which data structure allows deleting data elements from front and inserting at rear?
questions.explanation: A queue follows the First-In-First-Out (FIFO) principle, allowing deletion from the front (dequeue) and insertion at the rear (enqueue). This makes it ideal for scenarios where order needs to be maintained, such as task scheduling or message processing.

questions.questionText: What effect does achievement of quality attribute have on software product?
options: The achievement of quality attribute will always have a negative effect
The achievement of quality attribute will always have a positive effect
The achievement of quality attribute will have a positive as well as negative effect
questions.explanation: Achieving one quality attribute (e.g., security) might negatively impact another (e.g., performance). This is known as quality attribute trade-offs. For example, increasing security might reduce performance, while improving maintainability might increase development time. Software architects must carefully balance these trade-offs based on system requirements.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a type of independent malicious program that never requires any host program?
questions.explanation: Worms are standalone malware that don't need a host program to spread. They can replicate themselves and spread across networks independently. Unlike viruses that require a host program, worms are self-contained and can propagate through network vulnerabilities or social engineering.

questions.questionText: What layer functions as the basis for dialog control and synchronization?
questions.explanation: The Session Layer (Layer 5) manages dialog control and synchronization. It establishes, manages, and terminates connections between applications. The session layer provides services like dialog control, synchronization, and checkpointing to ensure proper communication between applications.

questions.questionText: What is the term used for a collection of large, complex data sets that cannot be processed using traditional data processing tools?
questions.explanation: Big data refers to datasets that are too large or complex for traditional data processing applications. It is characterized by the three Vs: Volume (large amounts of data), Velocity (high speed of data generation), and Variety (different types of data). Big data requires specialized tools and techniques for storage, processing, and analysis.

questions.questionText: A ______ is the lowest level of work on the project.
questions.explanation: A task is the smallest unit of work in project management.

questions.questionText: An ER diagram can express the overall ______ of a database graphically
questions.explanation: ER diagrams represent the logical structure of a database.

questions.questionText: Which design makes it most difficult to identify faults?
questions.explanation: Mesh networks have complex interconnections making fault isolation difficult.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not the contribution of the big data analysis
questions.explanation: Big data contributes to all the listed benefits (competitive advantage, market control, customer satisfaction).

questions.questionText: What does the HTTP status code 201 indicate?
questions.explanation: HTTP 201 means 'Created' - successful creation of a resource.

questions.questionText: Which of the following are famous and common cyber-attacks used by hackers to infiltrate the user's system?
questions.explanation: All listed methods are common cyber attack vectors. DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) attacks overwhelm systems, drive-by downloads install malware without user consent, malware/malvertising distribute malicious code, and phishing/password attacks steal credentials.

questions.questionText: Identify possible source(s) of unstructured data
questions.explanation: Twitter data (tweets) is unstructured, containing free-form text, images, videos, and links without a predefined data model. RDBMSs and database tables (options A, B, D) contain structured data with defined schemas.

questions.questionText: What type of CSS is generally recommended for designing large web pages?
questions.explanation: External CSS is preferred for large sites for better maintainability, reusability, and faster page loading through browser caching. It separates content from presentation and allows consistent styling across multiple pages.

The loop runs n times, and string concatenation (s = s + s[i]) is O(n) in C++ because it creates a new string and copies all characters. This results in O(n^2) total complexity as each iteration becomes more expensive as the string grows.

questions.questionText: The process to gather the software requirements from client analyze and document is known as
questions.explanation: Requirement engineering encompasses gathering, analyzing and documenting requirements. It includes elicitation, analysis, specification, validation, and management of requirements throughout the software development lifecycle.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following refers to the technique used for verifying the integrity of the message?
questions.explanation: Message digests (hashes) verify message integrity by detecting changes. They create a fixed-length unique fingerprint of data that changes if any part of the original message is altered, allowing recipients to verify the data hasn't been tampered with.

questions.questionText: What is the time complexity of the binary search algorithm?
questions.explanation: Binary search halves the search space each iteration, resulting in logarithmic complexity O(log2n). This makes it much more efficient than linear search for large sorted datasets.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not an activity lifecycle callback method?
questions.explanation: onClick() is an event handler for user interactions, not part of the Android Activity lifecycle. The Activity lifecycle callbacks include onCreate(), onStart(), onResume(), onPause(), onStop(), onDestroy(), and onRestart().

questions.questionText: What must be enabled in order for a RESTful web service to receive invocations from different domains, subdomains or ports?
questions.explanation: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) must be enabled for cross-domain requests. It's a security feature implemented by browsers that restricts web pages from making requests to domains other than the one that served the original page, unless the server explicitly allows it.

questions.questionText: Java's garbage collector carries out which of the following functions?
options: it frees up locations in memory that are no longer in use
it disposes of an applet once a web page is no longer visible
questions.explanation: Garbage collection automatically reclaims memory occupied by unreachable objects. It identifies objects that are no longer referenced by the program and frees the memory they occupy, preventing memory leaks and reducing manual memory management.
The code sums elements at even indices (0,2,4): a[0] + a[2] + a[4] = 1 + 3 + 5 = 9. The condition i % 2 == 0 selects indices 0, 2, and 4.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true of a class that has package scope?
options: class with package scope contains abstract methods only
class that has package scope is a source file and not a class file
only a class with package scope can be imported from the package
class with package scope is visible only to other classes within the same package
questions.explanation: Package-private (default) scope means the class is only visible within its package. When no access modifier is specified for a class in Java, it has package-private scope, making it accessible only to classes in the same package.

questions.questionText: In operating system, which mechanism is used to create process?
options: By calling a deadlock detection and recovery technique
Execution of a process creation system call by a running process
user request to create a new process
questions.explanation: Processes are created via system calls like fork() executed by existing processes. While system initialization (option D) does create initial processes, and user requests (option C) may trigger process creation, the actual mechanism is the execution of a system call by a running process.

questions.questionText: In Linux operating system, a process creates a child process using a system call:
questions.explanation: fork() is the system call used to create child processes in Linux. It creates a copy of the calling process, with the child process receiving a return value of 0 and the parent receiving the child's process ID as the return value.

questions.questionText: For a binary relationship set R between entity set A and B, the Mapping Cardinality is ONE TO ONE if
options: An Entity in A is associated with any number (zero or more) of entities in B, and an entity in B is associated with any number (zero or more) of entities in A
An Entity A is associated with any number (zero or more) of entities in B, an entity in B however, can be associated with at most one entity in A
An Entity in A is associated with at most one entity in B, and an entity in B is associated with at most one entity in A
An Entity A is associated with at most one entity in B, and an entity in B however, can be associated with any number (zero or more)of entities in A
questions.explanation: One-to-one means each entity in A relates to at most one entity in B, and each entity in B relates to at most one entity in A. This creates a direct pairing between entities, like a person and their unique social security number.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is just opposite to the Security through obscurity principle?
questions.explanation: Open design means security shouldn't depend on secrecy of design, opposite of security through obscurity. Open design advocates that system security should rely on the strength of its mechanisms rather than their secrecy, allowing public scrutiny to identify and fix vulnerabilities.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about local search algorithms is true?
options: The time complexity of local search algorithms is independent of the size of the problem
Local search algorithms are typically used for solving convex optimization problems
Local search algorithms always guarantee to find the globally optimal solution
The quality of the solution found by local search algorithms depends heavily on the starting point and the choice of the neighborhood function
questions.explanation: Local search performance depends on initial state and neighborhood definition, and may find local optima rather than global optima. These algorithms move from solution to solution in the search space by applying local changes, stopping when no better solutions can be found in the neighborhood.

questions.questionText: What keyword is used to declare an asynchronous function in Javascript?
questions.explanation: The 'async' keyword declares an asynchronous function in JavaScript. Async functions return promises and allow the use of 'await' to pause execution until a promise is resolved, making asynchronous code easier to write and understand.

questions.questionText: Android is ______
questions.explanation: Android is a mobile operating system based on Linux. It's designed primarily for touchscreen mobile devices like smartphones and tablets, and is developed by Google and the Open Handset Alliance.

questions.questionText: which of the following sorting algorithm is a divide-and-conquer type?
questions.explanation: Quick sort uses divide-and-conquer by partitioning the array and sorting subarrays recursively. It selects a 'pivot' element and partitions the array so elements less than the pivot come before it and elements greater come after, then recursively sorts the sub-arrays.

questions.questionText: What is the main disadvantage of uninformed search algorithms?
questions.explanation: Uninformed searches may find solutions but not necessarily the optimal one. Without heuristic information to guide them, algorithms like breadth-first or depth-first search explore paths without knowledge of which might lead to better solutions, often resulting in inefficient searches.

questions.questionText: Which SQL statement gives every employee a 10% raise.
questions.explanation: UPDATE is the SQL command for modifying existing data in a table. The correct syntax is 'UPDATE table_name SET column_name = value WHERE condition', though the WHERE clause is optional and omitted here to update all rows.

questions.questionText: Convert the following binary representation into dotted-decimal form: 10000000 00001011 00000011 00011111
Which of the following is not desired in a good software requirement specification(SRS) document
questions.explanation: An SRS should specify what the system should do, not how to implement it. Algorithms are implementation details that belong in design documents, not requirements. The SRS should focus on functional requirements, non-functional requirements, and goals, but leave implementation decisions to designers and developers.

questions.questionText: Under which of the following Android is licensed?
questions.explanation: Android is licensed under the Apache License, which is a permissive free software license written by the Apache Software Foundation. This allows developers to use, modify, and distribute Android code with minimal restrictions.

questions.questionText: What is the main advantage of informed search algorithms?
questions.explanation: The main advantage of informed search algorithms is that they are more efficient than uninformed searches because they use heuristic information to guide the search toward the goal. With an admissible heuristic, algorithms like A* are also optimal, guaranteeing the shortest path to the goal.

questions.questionText: Data generated for one use case may not be applicable to another use case. This describes which characteristic of Big Data?
questions.explanation: This describes Validity - ensuring that the data is correct and accurate for the intended use. Data valid for one purpose may not be valid for another, highlighting the context-dependent nature of data usefulness.

questions.questionText: A software system that manages a hotel booking system has been updated with a new feature that allows users to view room availability in real-time. A tester has been assigned to verify that existing functionality, such as the ability to book rooms and make payments, has not been adversely affected by the new feature. What type of testing is the tester performing?
questions.explanation: Regression testing ensures that new changes don't negatively impact existing functionality. The tester is specifically checking that old features still work after adding the new feature, which is the core purpose of regression testing.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between Dijkstra's Algorithm and Uniform Cost Search (UCS)?
options: Uniform Cost Search finds the optimal solution while Dijkstra's Algorithm doesn't
Dijkstra's Algorithm is optimal, but not UCS
Dijkstra's Algorithm first collects them into a Queue but UCS discover them as they come
Dijkstra's Algorithm discovers nodes as they come while UCS first collects them in a Queue
questions.explanation: The main difference is in node discovery - Dijkstra's uses a priority queue to explore nodes in order of increasing path cost, while UCS expands nodes as they are discovered. Both algorithms find optimal paths in graphs with non-negative edge weights.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is it NOT possible to do in Java?
options: execute more than one thread at a time
create arrays with more than two dimensions
questions.explanation: Java doesn't support direct pointer manipulation for safety and security reasons. While Java uses references internally, programmers cannot perform pointer arithmetic or directly access memory addresses as in languages like C or C++.

questions.questionText: Public key system is useful because
options: There is no key distribution problem as public key can be kept in a commonly accessible database
Private key can be kept secret
questions.explanation: Public key cryptography solves the key distribution problem of symmetric systems by allowing public keys to be freely shared while keeping private keys secret. This eliminates the need for a secure channel to exchange keys before communication.

The code alternates between adding (even indices) and subtracting (odd indices):
sum = +a[0]-a[1]+a[2]-a[3]+a[4] = +1-2+3-4+5 = 3

questions.questionText: What are some of the benefits of big data applications?
questions.explanation: Big data applications provide all these benefits by enabling analysis of large, complex datasets to uncover patterns, trends, and insights that can improve decision-making, customer understanding, and operational efficiency across organizations.

questions.questionText: ______ involves generating, collecting disseminating, and storing information.
questions.explanation: Communication Management is the process of generating, collecting, disseminating, and storing project information according to PMBOK (Project Management Body of Knowledge). It ensures timely and appropriate information flow among project stakeholders.

questions.questionText: A software testing professional has been asked to test a new feature for a client. However, the tester realizes that the feature is not working properly and may cause harm to the end-users. The client insists that the feature is released as scheduled, even though the tester has recommended further testing. What ethical principle from the ISTQB Code of Ethics should the tester follow in this situation?
questions.explanation: The Responsibility principle requires testers to act professionally and protect users from defective software, even when facing pressure to release. This includes reporting issues that could harm users and standing firm on quality standards.

questions.questionText: A software system that manages a hotel booking system has been updated with a new feature that allows users to view room availability in real-time. A tester has been assigned to verify that existing functionality, such as the ability to book rooms and make payments, has not been adversely affected by the new feature. What type of testing is the tester performing?
questions.explanation: This is regression testing - verifying that existing functionality still works after changes. Regression testing specifically focuses on ensuring that modifications haven't introduced new defects in previously working features.

questions.questionText: A ______ involves the team as a unit moving the ball down field in what would appear to be an ad hoc manner
questions.explanation: SCRUM is an agile framework where the team works collaboratively in sprints, adapting as they go - similar to a rugby team moving the ball downfield. The name 'Scrum' comes from rugby, where team members work together to move the ball forward.

questions.questionText: A good software requirement specification does not have the characteristics of
questions.explanation: Reliability is a quality of the implemented system, not the requirements specification. Good SRS characteristics include completeness, consistency, clarity, correctness, and verifiability, but reliability is an attribute of the final product, not the requirements document.

questions.questionText: In which process model, a number of dependent phases that are repeated sequentially with no feedback loops ______.
questions.explanation: The incremental model builds the product in sequential increments without feedback loops between phases. Each increment adds functionality to the previous version, but unlike iterative models, it doesn't revise or refine previous work based on feedback.

questions.questionText: What does ... operator do in Javascript?
options: Make a for loop execute three times
It is used to spread iterables to individual elements
It makes iterators continue with the increment interval
questions.explanation: The spread operator (...) expands an iterable (like an array) into individual elements. It can be used in array literals ([...arr]), function arguments (func(...arr)), and object literals ({...obj}) to copy or combine elements.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following memory management scheme is not used for mapping logical address into physical address?
questions.explanation: Swapping moves entire processes between memory and disk but doesn't handle address translation. It's a memory management technique for handling multiple processes, while paging and segmentation are specifically for mapping logical to physical addresses.

questions.questionText: Which of the following methods is used to access HTML elements using Javascript?
questions.explanation: getElementsByClassName() is a standard DOM method to access elements by class name. Other valid DOM methods include getElementById(), getElementsByTagName(), and querySelector(), but the other options in this question are not valid JavaScript methods.

questions.questionText: The cost of a project is computed by comparing the project to a similar project in the same application domain is called ______.
questions.explanation: Estimation by analogy compares the current project with similar past projects to derive cost estimates based on historical data. It's particularly useful when detailed requirements aren't yet available but similar projects exist.

questions.questionText: The specific set of sequential tasks upon which the project completion date depends or the longest full path is called ______.
questions.explanation: The critical path is the longest sequence of tasks that determines the shortest possible project duration. Any delay in tasks on the critical path directly delays the entire project completion date.

questions.questionText: What are the most important goals of software architecture?
options: Enable cost-effective integration and acceptance tests of the system.
Improve accuracy of patterns in structure and implementation
Enable a basic understanding of structures and concepts for the development team and other stakeholders.
To help understand the completeness of requirement
questions.explanation: A primary goal of software architecture is to provide a shared understanding of the system's structure for all stakeholders. This facilitates communication, guides implementation, and helps manage complexity in large systems.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is contained in the src folder?
questions.explanation: In standard project structures (like Maven or Android projects), the src folder contains source code files (Java, Kotlin, etc.). XML configuration files and manifests are typically stored in other directories like 'res' or project root.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT an objective of software testing?
questions.explanation: Testing aims to improve quality and find defects, not to increase development time. While thorough testing takes time, its purpose is to reduce overall development time by finding issues early when they're less expensive to fix.

questions.questionText: CPU fetches the instruction from memory according to the value of ______
questions.explanation: The program counter (PC) holds the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched and executed by the CPU. After fetching an instruction, the PC is automatically incremented to point to the next instruction.

questions.questionText: What is the first step in the data-driven decision-making process?
questions.explanation: The data-driven decision process begins with data collection, followed by analysis, interpretation, and finally decision-making. Without proper data collection, the subsequent steps cannot be performed effectively.

questions.questionText: Which of the following describes Triple DES?
options: Works with 144 bit blocks of plain text and applies DES algorithm once
Working on 64-bit blocks of plain text and 56 bit keys by applying des algorithm for three rounds
168 bit keys on 64-bit blocks of plain text
Uses 128 bit blocks of plain text and 112 bit keys and apply DES algorithm thrice.
questions.explanation: Triple DES (3DES) applies the DES cipher algorithm three times to each 64-bit block using either two or three 56-bit keys (168 bits total). It was developed as a more secure replacement for the original DES when computing power made DES vulnerable.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a checked exception
questions.explanation: Checked exceptions must be declared or caught (like IOException). They extend Exception but not RuntimeException. The other options are all unchecked exceptions that extend RuntimeException and don't require explicit handling.

questions.questionText: Which one is a false assumption to avoid race conditions to a problem of critical region?
options: No process running outside its critical region may block other processes
Assumptions should be made about speeds or the number of CPUs.
No process should have to wait forever to inter its critical region
No two processes may be simultaneously inside the critical regions.
questions.explanation: Correct solutions to critical section problems must make no assumptions about CPU speeds or numbers, as these are unpredictable.

questions.questionText: Which of the following informed search algorithms guarantees optimality when searching for a solution, but has an exponential time complexity in the worst-case scenario?
questions.explanation: A* search is optimal (with an admissible heuristic) but can have exponential time complexity in worst cases due to its search strategy.

questions.questionText: Which parameter is used to assess and evaluate software architectures?
options: Number of components in the Architecture
questions.explanation: Architectural quality attributes (like maintainability, performance, security) are the standard parameters used to evaluate software architectures, not just component count or responsiveness alone.

questions.questionText: What we use to pass the data between activities in Android?
questions.explanation: Intents are the Android mechanism for passing data between activities. Broadcast receivers handle system-wide events, content providers manage data sharing between apps, and databases are for persistent storage.
